messages:
maria-support: Heads up — Acme reported a spike of 503s on hosted inference starting ~2025-05-12T09:12Z. CS logs show gateway returning 503 with upstream: "run aborted". Noticed most failures during an authenticated batch that does toolcalling and long contexts. Attaching log excerpt below.

maria-support: ```
2025-05-12T09:12:03Z ERROR gateway request_id=acme-42 upstream_err='exit status 137' worker=inf-worker-7 node=gpu-pool-2
2025-05-12T09:12:03Z WARN runner: process terminated unexpectedly (signal SIGABRT)
2025-05-12T09:12:04Z INFO kernel: nvml: GPU 0 memory exceeded threshold, freeing caches
2025-05-12T09:12:04Z ERROR infer: kv-cache grew to 13.4GB > limit 12.0GB, triggering oom cleanup
```

gio-engineering: looking. can you paste the full request payload (sanitized) and whether this was streaming or non-streaming? did they call tools?

maria-support: payload is large chat batch (8 messages each ~7k tokens) + toolcall metadata. non-streaming, single request. sent sample sanitized payload to #eng-ml earlier. customer mentions this started after they increased per-request context lengths last week.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PDR-33421: hosted-infer.gpu-pool-2 runner-exit-rate > 5m threshold.

li-oncall: I'm on it, pulling runner logs and gcore. If this is kv-cache growth that's a new vector — could be prefetch retention leak on toolcall paths.

kevin-sre: quick mitigation ideas: 1) route Acme traffic to fallback smaller model (quantized) 2) throttle max_context or reject >8k tokens 3) bump worker memory limits for pool temporarily 4) enable prefix-cache eviction aggressively. Which can we flip fast?

gio-engineering: we can flip prefix eviction policy per-customer in ~5m (console toggle). I'll prepare a canary route to quant-6b.

li-oncall: repro plan — run stress harness against worker-7: `./tools/loadtest --host ${HOST} --concurrency 40 --requests 200 --payload samples/acme_longchat.json` — that recreated oom locally for me. attaching gdb bt from the crashing process.

li-oncall: ```
#0  0x00007f9a2c1b3f2a in __memcmp_sse4_1 () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6
#1  0x000055a1f3c4b2d6 in kv_cache::evict_range(…)
#2  0x000055a1f3c8c01a in runner::process_toolcall_stream(…)
#3  0x000055a1f3b6a7f8 in main_loop
```

maria-support: customer is on a paid enterprise plan; CS asked for ETA and workaround. They expressed billing concerns since requests succeeded intermittently and retried.

gio-engineering: root suspicion: toolcall path is retaining KV segments per-tool and not releasing on non-streaming completions. Long contexts + multiple tools -> kv cache fragmentation -> OOM. This is slightly different than normal batch size OOM.

kevin-sre: immediate actions completed: 1) created canary route to quant-6b for 10% of Acme traffic at 09:32Z 2) toggled prefix eviction to aggressive for Acme (TTL 30s) 3) raised gpu-pool-2 container memory limit + restarted worker-7. Observed reduced crash rate but still occasional restarts.

li-oncall: after restart we saw runner restart count drop from 12/min -> 2/min and 503s to gateway drop by ~85%. but one reproducer still causing segfault.

maria-support: CS informed customer of temporary routing + ask to reduce max_context for now. They want reproduction steps to pass to their devs.

gio-engineering: repro steps for customer/devs: 1) create a single non-streaming request with >6k token messages and 2 distinct toolcall entries that return 1-2k token outputs each 2) send as one batch of 6-8 similar requests in parallel 3) observe worker memory climb and potential 503s. Sample cURL: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME_KEY>" \n -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n -d @samples/acme_longchat.json --max-time 60
```

gio-engineering: mitigation patch queued: ensure kv segments created for toolcall are flagged for eager release on completion or if request is non-streaming. also add guardrails to limit kv allocation per-request. ETA for patch: ~24-36h, hotfix possible if we can reproduce deterministically.

kevin-sre: recommend customer-facing mitigation: 1) keep routing to quant-6b until patch 2) limit per-request context to 6k tokens 3) exponential retry with jitter on 5xx up to 3 attempts and surface billing credits if they hit >X failures.

maria-support: I'll coordinate CS message and propose one-time credit while we patch. Also scheduling a postmortem triage call at 13:00Z.

li-oncall: next steps for eng: 1) instrument kv allocator to track per-request usage and eviction timings (low effort) 2) reproduce deterministically with harness and attach ASAN if possible 3) temporary RBAC knob for aggressive eviction per-tenant.

gio-engineering: started branch `kv-eager-release` with tests. pushing logs and repro harness notes to the incident ticket.

maria-support: thanks all. CS will keep Acme updated; please ping here when hotfix is deployed so I can lift the routing and remove throttle. :thumbsup:

kevin-sre: ping when hotfix is on canary, I'll rollback memory bump once stable.

incident-bot: Incident note created: INC-2025-05-12-ACME-GPU-OOM-KV-BALLOON.

maria-support: closing loop for now — reduced customer impact, continuing debug.
